💪🏼Jeśli tęsknisz za tymi oldschoolowymi grami RTS, w których po prostu kierujesz swoją armię na wroga i obserwujesz chaos, ale nie chcesz mieć do czynienia z 47 różnymi zasobami, niekończącymi się drzewkami technologicznymi ani pilnowaniem 20 baz jednocześnie… to jest to coś dla Ciebie.

🪓💀 Crush Your Enemies to gra, w której ktoś wziął sedno zabawy klasycznych RTS-ów (budowanie wojsk, rozgrywka typu papier-kamień-nożyce, sprytne formacje) i pozbawił ją nudnego mikrozarządzania. Kontrolujesz hordę głośnych, wulgarnych barbarzyńców, którzy uwielbiają rozwalać twarze, pić i wykrzykiwać obelgi. Humor jest głupi, przerysowany i nieustannie rzuca żartami o rozbijaniu czaszek i plądrowaniu wszystkiego, co wpadnie im w oko. To gra, która ani przez chwilę nie traktuje siebie poważnie i właśnie dlatego działa. Rozgrywka jest niezwykle przystępna: szybkie gry, proste sterowanie, ale wciąż istnieje prawdziwa strategia w grupowaniu jednostek, momencie szarży i typach barbarzyńców do spamowania. Kampania dla jednego gracza jest solidna jak na swoją cenę, krótkie kampanie pełne absurdalnych celów.

🍖 Ogólnie rzecz biorąc, jak na swoją cenę (zwłaszcza w promocji), to świetna zabawa. Idealna, gdy chcesz szybkiej strategii bez poświęcania na nią całego wieczoru. Jeśli lubiłeś gry takie jak Totally Accurate Battle Simulator, albo po prostu lubisz krzyczeć na piksele, podczas gdy Twoi barbarzyńcy wykonują ciężką robotę, zdecydowanie spróbuj.
Polecam, zwłaszcza jeśli miałeś ciężki dzień i musisz pośrednio zmiażdżyć wrogów.

Crush Your Enemies, developed by Vile Monarch and published by Good Shepherd Entertainment, is a real-time strategy game that deliberately strips the genre down to its most essential elements. Instead of sprawling maps, endless unit types, and complex tech trees, it focuses on fast, bite-sized battles where the goal is simple: take territory, build a horde, and crush anyone who stands in your way. This design makes it approachable for newcomers to strategy games while still offering enough tactical decisions to keep each skirmish engaging. What sets it apart is not only its minimalist approach but also its irreverent tone, full of crude humor and tongue-in-cheek writing that leans into barbarian stereotypes and over-the-top antics.

The core gameplay revolves around capturing tiles on a grid-like map. Every match begins with a small group of barbarians, and success depends on how you spread them across neutral and enemy territory. Villages can be taken over to generate beer or troops, huts allow you to recruit different unit types, and specific structures provide upgrades or specialized functions. While the mechanics are simple, matches require constant micromanagement: deciding when to expand, when to hold ground, and when to commit troops to a fight. The pace is quick, and most battles end in minutes rather than hours, emphasizing speed and decisiveness over drawn-out planning. This design philosophy makes the game easy to pick up and play in short sessions while still delivering the feeling of commanding an army.

The single-player campaign spans around 40 levels and gradually introduces new mechanics, unit types, and scenarios. Bonus objectives in each mission encourage experimentation and replayability, though the campaign itself can be completed in just a handful of hours. While it doesn’t have the depth of a grand strategy title, the short runtime works in its favor, aligning with the game’s goal of being a quick, accessible strategy experience. Multiplayer is also included, offering the chance to test your skills against human opponents, but the online community has never been particularly large, meaning much of the long-term play will come from replaying the campaign or local skirmishes.

Where Crush Your Enemies distinguishes itself tonally is in its humor and presentation. The writing is crude, self-aware, and intentionally ridiculous, filled with jokes about beer, pillaging, and barbarian culture. The pixel art aesthetic is colorful and functional, ensuring that units and tiles are always easy to read during fast-paced play, even if the visuals are not especially detailed. The soundtrack and sound effects lean into the exaggerated style, with pounding drums and boisterous voice lines that match the game’s comedic barbarian theme. It is clear that the developers wanted the tone to be as lighthearted as the gameplay, making it hard to take anything too seriously.

That said, the simplicity of the design is also its biggest limitation. While the streamlined mechanics make it accessible, they also mean that after a few hours, strategies can start to feel repetitive. With only a handful of unit types and limited variations in maps, battles often play out in similar ways once you understand the optimal patterns of expansion and recruitment. The humor, while fun at first, can also wear thin over extended play sessions. Control responsiveness is another sticking point, especially when playing with a controller rather than a mouse, as the fast pace demands precise commands that can sometimes be difficult to execute smoothly.

Overall, Crush Your Enemies succeeds at what it sets out to do: deliver a condensed, chaotic, and funny version of real-time strategy. It is best enjoyed in short bursts, where its quick battles and crude humor shine brightest. For players looking for deep strategy systems or long campaigns, it may feel too shallow, but for those who want a casual RTS that can be played in minutes rather than hours, it offers a refreshing alternative. Its humor, fast pace, and accessible design make it an enjoyable experience, even if it is ultimately more of a light diversion than a lasting obsession.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Crush Your Enemies, Vile Monarch tarafından geliştirilen ve Good Shepherd Entertainment tarafından yayınlanan bir gerçek zamanlı strateji oyunudur. Oyun, oyuncuların düşman bölgelerini yağmalamak, talan etmek ve fethetmek için bir grup barbara liderlik ettiği Generia'nın fantezi dünyasında geçiyor. Oyun basit bir kontrol şemasına, çeşitli birim türlerine ve saatlerce süren stratejik oynanışa sahip tek oyunculu bir senaryoya sahiptir.

Oyunun seviyeleri derin stratejik seçeneklerle tasarlanmıştır, bu da zorlu ama ödüllendirici bir deneyim sağlar. Oyunun sistemlerinin karmaşıklığına rağmen, kontroller son derece basittir ve tek bir fare tuşuyla yönetilebilir. Tek oyunculu senaryo, saatlerce süren stratejik bir oyun deneyimi sunarak oyunun en önemli özelliklerinden biri.

Crush Your Enemies'in en çekici yönlerinden biri, hem PC hem de mobil cihazlarda arkadaşlarınıza ve sevdiklerinize karşı oynayabilmenizdir. Platformlar arası çok oyunculu oyun sayesinde savaş asla bitmek zorunda değil. Oyunda ayrıca her biri savaş alanında benzersiz bir role sahip farklı birim türleri ve savaşların gidişatını değiştirebilecek özel öğelerden oluşan yağmalanmış bir envanter bulunuyor.

Oyunun hikayesi yaramaz mizah, şiddet, bira ve küfürlerle doludur, bu da gönülsüz ve eğlenceli bir deneyim sağlar. Oyunun tuhaf boss savaşları, örneğin kafa kesme tutkusu olan dev bir ölüm salyangozuyla savaşmak, oyunun benzersiz ve keyifli oynanışına katkıda bulunuyor.

Genel olarak Crush Your Enemies, küçük bir pakette gerçek bir stratejik meydan okuma sağlayan mükemmel bir gerçek zamanlı strateji oyunudur. Basit kontrolleri, platformlar arası çok oyunculu özelliği ve eğlenceli hikayesiyle bu türün hayranları için mutlaka oynanması gereken bir oyun.

Crush Your Enemies is an absolute gem of a game! I think it's a fantastic blend of simplicity and challenge within the RTS genre. 

I really enjoy that the game takes traditional RTS gameplay elements and boils them down to something more akin to an 'arcade experience.' Familiar RTS concepts like resource management, unit recruitment, territory acquisition, and a 'rock-paper-scissors' combat balance are all present but have been greatly simplified. The 'bite-sized' game mechanics help keep matches fast-paced and short in duration while still allowing for a decent amount of strategic gameplay. 

The audio/visual presentation is quite nice but the 'story/dialogue' seems like it was written by a crass pre-teen (which is sort-of fitting to the theme I suppose as you do play as oafish barbarians).

- No ability to give commands during game pause
- Movig troops takes three clicks, which basically cuts your APM in half and often leads to accidental commands
- No hotkeys
- No ralley points
- An AI with unlimited APM, which will abuse that to create pincer attacks on multiple fronts, giving the player no real chance to react to everything appropriately

The combination of the above points leads to a very frustrating user experience, where the player has to restart the harder levels on basically every mistake

First of all, I will mention 2 flaws that most players find annoying in this game : 
1) Even a single mistake can potentially cause you to lose a mission and require to start the corresponding mission over -> IMHO, it's ok as most missions take fewer than 5 minutes to complete.
2) AI has much faster reaction and better unit control than you -> IMHO, you should deal with it. Yes, it's frustrating that your strategy would have worked if your AI had the same reaction as you, BUT there is always a strategy to beat AI even with its strengths. You should just find a strategy to overcome odds stacked against you.

CONCLUSION : Crush Your Enemies is a mix of an RTS and a puzzle game. The secret to beating the game is to be able to design a plan beforehand, to be able to execute it very fast and to be constantly aware of everything on the screen. All this would make the game unbeatable, but short length of missions allows you to rest between playing sessions.

一款独特且有趣的RTS游戏，非常值得一玩。建议打折入手。

很有策略性。操作要求中等。

价格：原价36元感觉略贵，折扣价3元的话肯定是超级实惠了。

AI在兵种选择、走位等方面感觉还挺聪明，AI兵营30人口就派出10人小队，这个肯定不是最聪明的方法，不过这应该是让着玩家。毕竟AI反应速度碾压人类，再使用最优策略的话，玩家得怒而弃游了。

有人吐槽这游戏的操作。我刚打完第一章，感觉操作并不怎么难。红警、星际、全球行动、铁锈战争等RTS游戏，操作量比这个游戏还要大很多好吗？这个游戏操作兵种的步骤为：单击一下选中一组（一个格子内，1-50人），再点击一下目标点，然后在目标点（即目标方格）上弹出一个小界面，可以点击上边显示的三个数字选择移动单位的数量，也可以拖动滑条选择数量。因此，操作部队移动或者攻击等，只需要三个动作，选择单位、选择目标点，选择数量。过程中可以点击鼠标右键取消选择。而且，如果是全选一组单位，那么第二次点击和第三次可以通过快速双击完成。

传统的RTS游戏，完成上述操作i，不编队的情况下三次点击能完成？而且传统RTS游戏还要拖动视野然后点击目标点，而这个游戏全地图都在一个屏幕之内。

另外，玩游戏时不要完全按照游戏教程里教的策略玩。游戏教程里教的分队、近战和远程部队配合，真的不是什么好策略，而且操作繁琐。两个50人口远程小队，轻松吊打一个50人口远程+一个50人口近战的队伍。因为两个远程部队可以相互掩护。远程被打是近战部队只能干瞪眼。
